title: Payment issues bother north Indian cotton yarn, demand slows
summary:
North India's cotton yarn markets stayed stable in Ludhiana, Delhi and Panipat as weak demand and tight payments curbed fresh buying.
Downstream textile and garment output has yet to normalise after Diwali, though traders expect summer garmenting and winter retail demand to improve.
Cotton eased ₹20-30 per maund after weaker ICE futures, with new arrivals at 10,500 bales.

title: Will costlier acrylonitrile keep acrylic fibre above $2.5/kg?
summary:
China’s acrylic staple fibre prices rose in the first week of November 2026 before flattening, as higher acrylonitrile costs reached the fibre market.
Between November 2 and 13, 1.5D*38mm gained 3.6 per cent to $2.529/kg, while 3D*68mm rose 3.3 per cent to $2.518/kg.
Crude oil and propylene moved lower, but buyers resisted further increases.

title: India begins pre-budget consultations amid growth, inflation concerns
summary:
Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman began pre-budget consultations with leading economists ahead of the Union Budget 2027-28, amid concerns over inflation and a possible slowdown in second-quarter economic growth. 
The government is scheduled to release July-September GDP data on November 30. 
The Budget is expected to be presented on February 1, 2027.

title: Swedish textile firms to showcase innovations at India ITME forum
summary:
Swedish textile technology companies will showcase automation and resource-efficient solutions at the Sweden-India Textile Technology & Innovation Forum on 7 December 2026 in Greater Noida.
Organised by Business Sweden and TMAS with CITI alongside India ITME, the event will connect suppliers, manufacturers and brands through technology presentations, industry discussions and business networking.

title: India & Egypt to explore trade pact terms as trade rises 65%
summary:
India and Egypt have agreed to form a Joint Working Group to explore terms for a preferential or free trade agreement after the 7th Joint Trade Committee met at ministerial level. 
Bilateral trade rose 35 per cent to $6.5 billion in FY 2025-26 and 65 per cent to $5.04 billion in April-September 2026. 
Textiles were among priority sectors for trade, investment and joint manufacturing.

title: Lululemon's enzymatic polyester: Can recycling scale beyond 0.3%?
summary:
Lululemon’s shorts capsule uses at least 50 per cent enzymatically recycled polyester, but feedstock, volumes and prices are undisclosed.
It does not confirm textile-to-textile content; buyers should verify origin, traceability and capacity.
Textile-to-textile recycled polyester was 0.3 million tonnes in 2025, 0.3 per cent of total output; 97 per cent of recycled polyester was bottle-based.

title: Bangladesh's cotton imports to rise to 7.5 mn bales in MY 2027: USDA
summary:
Bangladesh's cotton imports are projected to rise 1.35 per cent to 7.5 million bales in MY27, driven by growing spinning industry demand, according to the USDA. 
Brazil is expected to remain the largest supplier, while Bangladesh will rank as the world's second-largest importer after Vietnam. 
India's share is forecast to hold at 15 per cent, while US and Australian supplies are expected to increase.

title: Trützschler brings smarter spinning solutions to India ITME 2026
summary:
Trützschler will showcase spinning, card clothing and nonwovens innovations at India ITME 2026 in Greater Noida.
Highlights include the TC 26i intelligent card, TCO 21XL 12-head comber, automated can transport and digital services.
At Hall 11, Booth B15, visitors can explore technologies designed to boost productivity, improve fibre utilisation, reduce costs and ensure consistent quality.

title: Barmag enhances specialty yarn production at India’s Garden Silk Mills
summary:
India’s Garden Silk Mills has retrofitted 24 WINGS FDY polyester spinning positions with Barmag’s single-stage Bi-Shrinkage Yarn concept.
Based on WINGS FDY PLUS eco, the technology delivers high yarn quality, productivity and low waste.
It combines POY and FDY in one spinning process, helping the company meet growing demand for specialty yarns used in apparel and home textiles.

title: China's industrial output grows 4.8%, retail sales edge up 0.4%
summary:
China’s industrial value-added rose 4.8 per cent year on year in October, with manufacturing up 5.4 per cent and high-tech manufacturing up 17.6 per cent, official data showed.
Consumer goods retail sales reached 4,646.3 billion yuan (~$696 billion), up 0.4 per cent year on year.
Online retail sales of goods rose 2.9 per cent in the first ten months.

title: Bangladesh's apparel exports to EU fall 11.9% in January-September
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU fell 11.91 per cent year on year to €13.48 billion (~$14.81 billion) in January-September 2026, Eurostat data showed.
The drop was the steepest among the bloc’s 11 largest suppliers; volume fell 5.74 per cent and unit price dropped 6.54 per cent.
China gained share, while overall EU apparel imports fell 2.46 per cent to €70.72 billion (~$77.71 billion).

title: US' Nike teams up with universities to boost female athlete safety
summary:
Nike has launched Project Shield: Protect to Perform with Stanford’s Wu Tsai Human Performance Alliance, Emory University and the University of Oregon to advance research and injury prevention for female athletes.
The initiative combines prospective research, implementation science and AI-based movement analysis, while Nike pilots the NSRL Form for Field app for football players.

title: South Korea’s Misto Holdings posts 3.4% revenue rise in Q3
summary:
Misto Holdings' third-quarter revenue rose 3.4 per cent YoY to ₩1.1 trillion (~$823.41 million), although operating profit fell 3 per cent to ₩128 billion (~$95.81 million). 
Its Misto segment lifted revenue 15.1 per cent, aided by Malaysian demand and Korean apparel sales. 
Acushnet revenue grew 1.1 per cent as Titleist golf balls benefited from higher prices and volumes.

title: AAFA urges worker rights safeguards in Bangladesh garment sector
summary:
The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged Bangladesh to ensure an inclusive and transparent minimum wage review for garment workers, with safeguards against violence, intimidation and retaliation. 
It called for annual wage revisions, stronger worker protections, effective tripartite consultations and responsible purchasing practices by international brands and retailers.

title: Cambodia’s apparel exports reach at $10 bn in January-October 2026
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports rose 6.31 per cent YoY to $10.223 billion in January–October 2026, remaining the country’s largest export earner.
Shipments made up 34.1 per cent of total merchandise exports, with knitted apparel up 4.3 per cent and non-knitted apparel up 10.9 per cent.
Cotton and cotton yarn imports surged 29.5 per cent, signalling stronger demand for cotton-based manufacturing.

title: Bangladesh's garment factories shut amid protests over wage hike
summary:
Wage protests have halted more than 100 garment factories in Gazipur, Ashulia and Savar, with 11 units announcing indefinite closures ahead of Bangladesh's minimum wage talks.
Workers proposed Tk32,000 (~$256) a month, while employers may submit a proposal but boycott Monday's Minimum Wage Board meeting.
RMG accounts for around 80 per cent of Bangladesh's $48 billion in annual exports.

title: 5.4% of US importers face a new customs rule: What changes in 2027?
summary:
US apparel companies under DDP terms should review import arrangements before CBP's foreign-IOR rule takes effect on January 5, 2027.
Foreign IORs must be CTPAT-validated or use a CTPAT-validated licensed broker, which must act as IOR when the principal is not owner or purchaser.
CBP cited $1.16 billion in unpaid foreign-IOR duties from 2020 to August 2026, with only $35.7 million collected.

title: US’ Wolverine posts eighth consecutive quarter of growth in Q3 FY26
summary:
Wolverine World Wide has raised its FY26 outlook after third-quarter revenue rose 7.5 per cent to $505.4 million and net earnings attributable to the company reached $65.8 million.
Operating margin expanded to 17.7 per cent, aided by $35.3 million in IEEPA tariff refunds.
The footwear and apparel group now expects FY26 revenue of $2.00-$2.01 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.95-$1.99.

title: India's $1 bn US apparel gap: Can exporters win back buyers?
summary:
TexPro found India's US apparel imports fell $1.014 billion in January-August 2026, down 25.96 per cent as the market slipped 7.02 per cent.
Its share fell to 5.59 per cent from 7.02 per cent, while Vietnam and Cambodia gained and knitted apparel led losses.
Talks may ease clearance, but no apparel-specific tariff relief is confirmed; recovery hinges on price, delivery and policy stability.

title: US' AAFA welcomes Senate passage of Customs Notification Act
summary:
AAFA has welcomed US Senate passage of the Customs Notification Act (H.R. 4930), saying it would strengthen CBP’s ability to share information with brands and stakeholders. 
The measure covers products, packaging and packing materials linked to suspected counterfeit shipments during IP enforcement. 
AAFA president and CEO Steve Lamar urged President Trump to sign it into law.
